title: Commit message validation
responsibility: Cleans a hook message as Git would and reports stored-message prefix and length violations.

inputs.name: writtenMessage.file
inputs.description: The complete text Git gives to a commit-msg hook. The function treats it as message text and never reads a filesystem path.
examples:
feat: add retries

Retry transient errors.
# Please enter the commit message

inputs.name: writtenMessage.options
inputs.description: Cleanup mode and comment marker for writtenMessage; omitted fields default to cleanup = 'strip' and comment = '#'. Verbatim trims only the ends, while every other mode cuts at scissors and whitespace or scissors mode keeps comment lines.

inputs.name: commitMessage.message
inputs.description: The stored commit message text, split into a first subject line and the remaining body lines. CRLF and lone CR line endings become LF, and the joined body is trimmed before validation.
examples:
fix: handle missing values

Reject empty input.

outputs.name: commitPrefixes
outputs.description: The four allowed subject prefix tokens: feat:, fix:, chore:, and cleanup:. The list contains the tokens only; a valid nonempty subject must also have a space and a nonspace character after one of them.

outputs.name: writtenMessage
outputs.description: The hook message after cleanup: non-verbatim modes cut at a line beginning with the configured comment marker and scissors marker, remove comment lines except in whitespace and scissors modes, remove matched trailing spaces, tabs or carriage returns, collapse runs of three or more LF newlines to two, and trim the ends. Verbatim returns file.trim() and preserves internal text.
examples:
feat: add retries

Retry transient errors.

outputs.name: commitMessage
outputs.description: Returns the subject and body length problems produced by writingProblems using writingLimits.subject and writingLimits.body, plus a missing-prefix problem for a nonempty subject unless it starts with one of the four allowed prefixes, a colon and space, and a following nonspace character. An empty subject is reported through the subject length checks; the body is checked only when its joined, trimmed text is nonempty, and an empty result means no problems were reported.
examples: subject does not start with feat:, fix:, chore: or cleanup:.
